description: A coalition of mid-sized EU member states, frustrated by the paralysis of central coordination and recent access denials, begins informal coordination with South Korea, Japan, and Canada on mutual compute access and evaluation standards. The network operates through technical working groups rather than formal treaties, focusing on fallback access to non-frontier but high-capability models in case of future disruptions. It is not yet a policy initiative, but a quiet hedge gaining momentum among digital ministers.

An unexpected efficiency breakthrough in sparse model training—discovered in a joint German-Swiss research lab—demonstrates that models at 58.0 capability can now be trained with 40% less compute. The method spreads rapidly through open research channels, accelerating the openweight trajectory. If sustained, it could compress the closed-open gap without requiring new hardware. The labs involved publish cautiously, citing dual-use concerns, but the algorithm is already being replicated.
